conventions.convention: The spaces are real Hilbert spaces; F is Fréchet differentiable on an open domain, and F' is continuous in operator norm. Countable Choice is assumed for Hilbert adjoints.

The exact solution lies in the closed radius-r ball about x₀; the closed radius-2r outer ball lies in U. On the outer ball, derivative norms are at most 1 and the two-point cone inequality holds uniformly, with derivative based at the first point and one shared 0 ≤ η < 1/2.
The discrepancy parameter satisfies τ > 2(1+η)/(1−2η). Indices start at zero; the residual test uses ≤ τδ and precedes the finite-budget test, including when M=0.

Fejér monotonicity means nonincrease of distance to the stated exact solution. Finite discrepancy stopping is asserted for δ>0; exact-data convergence does not assert finite stopping or minimum-norm selection.
The stalling counterexample studies the update formula as a bare recurrence, rather than claiming an admissible run of the defined algorithm.

load_bearing.statement: For an admissible local instance and finite update budget M, start at x₀, test the residual against τδ before testing the budget, and otherwise update by xₖ₊₁δ=xₖδ+F'(xₖδ)*(yδ−F(xₖδ)). Return either stopped with the index, iterate and residual, or budget_exhausted with the last iterate and residual.

Under Countable Choice, the stated real-Hilbert differentiability and operator-norm continuity assumptions, an exact solution within radius r of x₀, derivative norm at most 1 and uniform two-point TCC with η<1/2 on the closed radius-2r ball contained in U, noise bounded by δ, and τ>2(1+η)/(1−2η): the stated squared-error estimate gives Fejér decrease before discrepancy stopping; for δ>0 the first stop N exists with N<Cδ⁻², C=1+d₀²/(cττ²); the exact-data sequence is globally defined, has (1−2η)Σ‖F(xₙ)−y‖²≤d₀², and converges strongly to an exact solution x̄ in the outer ball; noisy stopped iterates converge to that same x̄ uniformly over the admissible noise ball as δ decreases to zero. Finite-budget output conclusions require the stated comparison of M with N.

published_dependencies.used_for: Bounded real-linear derivatives, the pointwise derivative map, and differentiability implying continuity.
Cauchy-sequence completeness in the exact-data strong convergence argument.
Real inner-product symmetry, induced norm and squared-norm expansion.
Adjoint existence under Countable Choice and the adjoint pairing identity.
Boundedness and norm equality for adjoints, including continuity of the adjoint action.
The explicit choice assumption for adjoints and selection of a sequence of bad noisy data.
Pairing bounds in the one-step estimate and the exact-data Cauchy argument.
Triangle inequalities for residuals, localization and convergence.
Zero-based nonnegative series, partial sums and tails.
Convergence of bounded nonnegative residual-square and squared-error-drop series; vanishing tails follow elementarily.
Real completeness supporting the scalar convergence arguments.
Choosing a sufficiently large positive number of updates to contradict perpetual failure of the discrepancy test.
Least stopping indices, least residual minimizers on finite blocks, and canonical subsequence choices.

concerns.concern: Proof 4.2 asserts Kτ²δ² < Σ_{n<K}(Rₙδ)² for every natural K. At K=0 this reads 0<0. Restrict this strict inequality to K≥1; the Archimedean contradiction only needs positive K.

Proof 9.1 says 'for every j' select a positive δⱼ<1/j without specifying j≥1. The library's natural-number indexing includes zero, where 1/j is undefined. Start this auxiliary sequence at j=1 or use 1/(j+1).
